texts: bad: what Pell said is lost — a comparative with no stated standard ('weaker' than what?) has to be dropped, and 'fewer nightmoths' as a bare plural has no carrier for the 'fewer', so the covariation has no licensed form at all; the parse currently records Pell as saying the unqualified 'lanterns draw nightmoths', which is a wider claim than he made. Rewrite with an explicit standard and one finite clause per compared case: 'On day 17 of Year 1, Pell told Coraline Ash at midnight that a dim lantern draws fewer nightmoths than a bright lantern draws.' The telling itself — Pell, Coraline Ash, midnight, day 17 of Year 1 — already parses correctly and needs no change.

bad: the same loss — with 'fewer' on both sides there is no licensed form, so the complement comes out as the bare claim 'nightmoths leave silken threads', dropping the proportionality that is the whole point. Rewrite as 'Pell told Coraline Ash that a small swarm of nightmoths leaves fewer silken threads than a large swarm leaves.' — a comparison stated between two named cases is encodable where a bare covariation is not.

bad: the same loss a third time — 'fewer silken threads yield less mire-essence' comes out as the unqualified 'silken threads yield mire-essence', with both 'fewer' and 'less' dropped. Rewrite as 'Pell told Coraline Ash that a small bundle of silken threads yields less mire-essence than a large bundle yields.'; counting the yield in vessels ('fewer vessels of mire-essence than a large bundle yields') parses even more cleanly, since the comparison is then over countable things.

good. the writing event, Coraline Ash as its author, the notebook and the past tense are all carried, the four definite participants are typed outside the report, and the claim itself is held as one forming event with all four as participants and the closed loop inside it — it stays usable in place once the three preceding reports are rewritten.
